panels.title: Repositories collected
panels.description: Current total across all sources. Not affected by the time range.

panels.title: By source
panels.description: Current row counts. Four similar magnitudes, so bars rather than a pie.

panels.title: Data quality
panels.description: Share of stored rows passing the same checks the pipeline runs: an http url, a creation date that isn't in the future, and a non-negative star count. Computed from the data rather than from run counters, which live and die with the job pod.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE url LIKE 'http%' AND (created_at IS NULL OR created_at <= now()) AND stars >= 0) / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_rate FROM analytics_marts.fct_repositories

panels.title: Exporter pods
panels.description: Autoscales between 2 and 5. Two is the healthy floor, not a scaled-down failure.

panels.title: Hours since last extraction
panels.description: The one panel here that constitutes alerting. Climbing on every source at once means the scheduled job has stopped running, which fails silently otherwise.

panels.title: Errors per second
panels.description: From the metrics exporter. The extraction job's own counters exit with its pod, so a quiet line here means the exporter is healthy, not that nothing ever fails.

panels.title: Popular but going stale
panels.description: High star count, no commit in six months, and not archived. Archived is excluded on purpose: the maintainers announcing they have stopped is a different thing from nobody having touched it, and this panel is about the second. Including them put atom at the top of the neglect list, when GitHub retired it deliberately. Read from staging rather than the mart, which does not carry the flag. Empty is a good result on a small sample of top repositories.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name, language, stars, days_since_update AS days_stale FROM analytics_staging.stg_repositories WHERE stars > 5000 AND days_since_update > 180 AND NOT archived ORDER BY days_since_update DESC LIMIT 12

panels.title: Most starred
panels.description: Current snapshot from the marts. Not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name, language, stars, stars_per_fork AS per_fork FROM analytics_marts.fct_repositories WHERE stars > 0 ORDER BY stars DESC LIMIT 12

panels.title: Top languages
panels.description: GitHub and GitLab only. PyPI is excluded deliberately: every package there is Python by definition, so counting those rows measures which registry a project came from rather than what it is written in. Including them put Python at 619 against TypeScript's 80, of which 502 were PyPI saying nothing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT language_display AS language, starred_count AS repositories FROM analytics_marts.dim_languages WHERE starred_count > 0 ORDER BY starred_count DESC, language LIMIT 10

panels.title: Momentum
panels.description: Growth, download velocity and decayed attention combined. Each component is shown next to the total because the weights are guesses, and signals says how many could be measured at all - a source that cannot report one is not scored down for it. Needs about a week of history before growth contributes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.name, r.source, m.momentum, m.growth_component AS growth, m.attention_component AS attn, m.signals_measured AS signals FROM analytics_marts.fct_momentum m JOIN raw_repositories r ON r.id = m.repository_id WHERE m.momentum IS NOT NULL ORDER BY m.momentum DESC LIMIT 15

panels.title: Fastest growing
panels.description: Stars gained, from the snapshot history. Absolute and rate together, because 200 to 400 is a doubling and 200,000 to 200,200 is noise. The 7-day column stays empty until there are seven days of snapshots.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.name, r.source, g.stars, g.stars_gained_1d AS "+1d", g.stars_gained_7d AS "+7d", g.stars_growth_pct_7d AS "%7d", g.days_observed AS days FROM analytics_marts.fct_repository_growth g JOIN raw_repositories r ON r.id = g.repository_id WHERE g.stars_gained_1d IS NOT NULL ORDER BY g.stars_gained_1d DESC LIMIT 15

panels.title: 7-day forecast
panels.description: TimesFM zero-shot, gated on real history: a repository with fewer than 14 observed days shows as insufficient_history rather than a fabricated number. p10/p90 is the model's own uncertainty band, not a fixed confidence interval - see docs/specs/2026-08-15-timesfm-forecasting-design.md.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.name, f.baseline_stars, f.predicted_stars_p50, (f.predicted_stars_p50 - f.baseline_stars) AS predicted_gain, f.predicted_stars_p10, f.predicted_stars_p90, f.suppressed_reason FROM repository_forecasts f JOIN raw_repositories r ON r.id = f.repository_id WHERE f.horizon_days = 7 AND f.forecast_date = (SELECT max(forecast_date) FROM repository_forecasts) ORDER BY predicted_gain DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 15

panels.title: Being discussed but not tracked
panels.description: The discovery queue. Projects people are linking that the dataset does not contain - which is what the seeding, being ranked by cumulative popularity, excludes by construction. Anything clearing the score floor gets fetched on the next run. Owner is blank for npm and PyPI rows: a package page names one artifact and has no owner in its URL, so the column is empty rather than repeating the package name. The project name links out to the page it came from.

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN split_part(target_url, '/', 3) IN ('github.com', 'gitlab.com') THEN split_part(target_url, '/', 4) END AS owner, CASE WHEN split_part(target_url, '/', 3) IN ('github.com', 'gitlab.com') THEN split_part(target_url, '/', 5) WHEN split_part(target_url, '/', 3) IN ('npmjs.com', 'pypi.org') THEN nullif(regexp_replace(target_url, '^https://[^/]+/(package|project)/', ''), '') END AS project, split_part(target_url, '/', 3) AS host, posts, decayed_score AS decayed, target_url FROM analytics_marts.fct_undiscovered_mentions ORDER BY decayed_score DESC LIMIT 12

value.title: Open the page this was linked from

panels.title: Found by being discussed
panels.description: Projects that entered the dataset because people were talking about them, rather than because they were already popular enough to be seeded. Recorded separately because a discovered set is selected by having been discussed, which is a bias on anything computed from it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name, source, stars, created_at::date AS created, loaded_at::date AS found FROM raw_repositories WHERE origin = 'discovered' ORDER BY loaded_at DESC, stars DESC LIMIT 12

panels.title: Field coverage by source
panels.description: Which fields each source actually populates. Check this before comparing anything across sources - npm reports no stars, GitHub and GitLab report no downloads, and averaging across them gives a number that means nothing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT source, repository_count AS rows, with_stars AS stars, with_downloads AS downloads, with_language AS language, round(avg_days_since_update) AS stale FROM analytics_marts.dim_sources ORDER BY source

panels.title: Stars gained per day, by language
panels.description: Which language ecosystems are attracting attention, day by day. Counting repositories per language instead would draw a flat line: projects are never removed from the tracked set, so the mix only accumulates and cannot show one language displacing another. Stars move daily, so this does. The first day is null rather than zero - there is nothing to subtract from - and PyPI is excluded for the same reason as the bar chart above. Treat a single day as noise; the shape needs a week.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, metric, value FROM (SELECT s.captured_on::timestamp AS time, r.language AS metric, sum(s.stars) - lag(sum(s.stars)) OVER (PARTITION BY r.language ORDER BY s.captured_on::timestamp) AS value FROM repository_snapshots s JOIN raw_repositories r ON r.id = s.repository_id WHERE r.language IS NOT NULL AND r.source IN ('github', 'gitlab') AND r.language IN (SELECT language FROM raw_repositories WHERE language IS NOT NULL AND source IN ('github', 'gitlab') GROUP BY language ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 8) GROUP BY 1, 2) d WHERE value IS NOT NULL ORDER BY time, metric

panels.title: Approximate spend per day
panels.description: Dollars, priced from the token counts the API reports against published per-million rates. Approximate on purpose: it is our arithmetic rather than the invoice, and it is wrong the day pricing changes - but a cost panel with a real counter behind it beats the alternative, which was a panel querying a metric nobody emitted. That renders an empty graph, and an empty graph looks exactly like no spend.

panels.title: Tokens per day
panels.description: Input and output kept apart, because they are priced five times differently - a rise in output tokens costs far more than the same rise in input, and a combined line hides which one moved.

panels.title: Answer quality over time
panels.description: Faithfulness and relevance as separate series, and they must stay separate. A low faithfulness score is an invented answer; a low relevance score is a dull one. Averaging them into a single quality number loses the only distinction worth acting on. Gaps are runs where the judge could not be reached - those are stored as null rather than zero, so the line breaks instead of dropping to the floor.

targets.rawSql: SELECT evaluated_at AS time, 'faithfulness' AS metric, faithfulness AS value FROM rag_evaluations WHERE faithfulness IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(evaluated_at) UNION ALL SELECT evaluated_at AS time, 'relevance' AS metric, relevance AS value FROM rag_evaluations WHERE relevance IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(evaluated_at) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Hallucination rate
panels.description: The share of evaluated answers that failed faithfulness, against a target of under 2%. Answers the judge could not score are excluded from both halves of the fraction rather than counted as good - and with nothing scored at all this reads No data rather than 0%, because a rate computed from no evaluations is not perfection.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE hallucination) / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE hallucination IS NOT NULL), 0), 1) AS "Hallucination %" FROM rag_evaluations

panels.title: Questions asked, and how many skipped a rebuild
panels.description: Questions by the confidence the model committed to, alongside context cache results. A hit means the retrieved context was reused rather than rebuilt from the marts. Cache outages are counted apart from misses: both end in a database query, but one is the cache working and the other is the cache being gone, and a hit rate that folds them together is a hit rate about nothing.
